To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the current TNM staging system has been shown to be inadequate for predicting survival for patients with rectal cancer, and that the current system is also inadequate in predicting the risk of local recurrence.
the current TNM staging system is based on a series of arbitrary decisions that are no longer justified, and that the time has come for a radical overhaul of the system.
(a) the accuracy of the staging of rectal cancers is poor, and (b) the accuracy of staging is not improved by the use of multiple staging systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an evidence‐based approach to the staging of cancer.
the development and evaluation of evidence‐based staging systems.
the use and interpretation of staging in the context of evidence‐based medicine, and the development and validation of staging systems for colorectal cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the time has come for the staging of cancers to be based on the most appropriate and accurate evidence available.
the time has come for a consensus on staging, and that the way forward is through the establishment of a working group to define standards.
staging is not an exact science and should not be treated as such.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need to improve staging and to do so we need to develop a staging classification system that is based on the best available evidence.
it is not necessary to set standards for cancer staging.

the time has come for the pathologist to be the lead clinician in the management of cancer patients, to be the leader in cancer research and to be the leader for the development of evidence‐based standards for cancer staging.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be more explicit about the staging system used and to be more rigorous in our reporting of the staging of colorectal cancer.
the time has come for a radical overhaul of the way in which we stage colorectal cancer.
there is a need for standardization in reporting of staging information in the pathology report.
